---
title: "LIBERTY: a bug in the original paper, and its fix"
---

```{python}
from _lib import *
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots
from leafrtm.rtm import get_model
from leafrtm.rtm.liberty import ABSORBERS, _cell, _slab_m_np

fixed, pub = get_model("liberty"), get_model("liberty_dawson")
screen = read("fit_screen")
fits = read("liberty_fits")
if len(screen):
    screen = screen[screen["model"] == "liberty"]
BRIGHT = dict(xu=0.04, thick=1.8, baseline=0.0004, element=0.5, c_factor=200, w_factor=100, l_factor=40,
              p_factor=1)
NIR = int(np.argmin(abs(fixed.wavelength - 800)))
C_FIX, C_PUB = MODEL_COLOR["liberty"], MODEL_COLOR["liberty_dawson"]


def rinf_plane(model, xu, k, i=NIR):
    """R_inf at band i for cell absorption coefficient k (NaN where it has no real root)."""
    x, Tt = _cell(model.mi[i], xu, _slab_m_np(k))
    with np.errstate(invalid="ignore"):
        return model._layer(model.me[i], x, Tt, np)[2]
```

**Summary.** LIBERTY (Dawson et al. 1998), as published, has no solution for bright leaves.
The cause is an algebra error in the paper: its closed-form equation for the reflectance of an
infinitely thick leaf (Eq. 16) is not the sum of the series it is derived from (Eq. 15). Every
LIBERTY result on this site uses `liberty`, which fixes this bug. The published model is kept,
as `liberty_dawson`, for comparison only.

| Name in the code | What it is | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `liberty` | LIBERTY with Eq. 16 replaced by the correct sum of Eq. 15 | all fits and analyses |
| `liberty_dawson` | LIBERTY as published, and as implemented in `rrtm` | this page only |

Both variants also share a second, smaller correction, to the internal reflectance of the cell
wall (see [below](#a-second-correction-the-internal-reflectance-m_i)).

## How LIBERTY works

LIBERTY treats a leaf as layers of spherical cells. Inside the leaf, light at each wavelength
is either absorbed in a cell or scattered at a cell wall. Two quantities control it:

* **Scattering, through `xu`:** the intercellular air-space determinant, the fraction of light
  that leaves a cell towards the air spaces.
* **Absorption, through the per-cell transmission $\tau$:** this depends on the cell absorption
  coefficient $k(\lambda) = D\,[\text{baseline} + \sum_j K_j(\lambda)\,C_j]$, where $K_j$ are
  the specific absorption coefficients of chlorophyll, water, lignin and cellulose, protein
  and "albino" material, and $C_j$ are their concentrations.

The model first finds the reflectance $R_\infty$ of an infinitely thick stack of cells. It then
uses $R_\infty$ to get the reflectance and transmittance of one layer, and stacks layers to the
leaf's thickness.

$R_\infty$ is set by a self-consistency condition: putting one more layer of cells on top of an
infinitely thick leaf must not change its reflectance. Dawson et al. (Fig. 1, Eq. 15) write this
as a series. Light reaching the leaf is either reflected by the top layer of cells, or passes
through that layer, is reflected by the leaf below, and comes back up through the top layer,
possibly after more bounces.

## The bug

The correct sum of the Eq. 15 series is

$$R_\infty = 2xm_e + \frac{x(1-2xm_e)\,\tau\,(1-m_eR_\infty)}{(1-m_eR_\infty) - (1-x)(1-m_e)\,\tau R_\infty},$$

where $m_e$ is the reflectance of the cell surface for light arriving from outside, and $x$ the
upward-scattering fraction (a function of `xu` and $\tau$). Clearing the denominator gives a
quadratic in $R_\infty$.

To clear the denominator, Eq. 16 puts the first term, $2xm_e$, over the common denominator
without multiplying it by that denominator. `rrtm`, and so `liberty_dawson`, implement Eq. 16
as printed.

The two equations behave very differently:

* **The correct sum** is the "adding" equation for one layer of cells that loses light only by
  absorption. It therefore always has a solution, and $R_\infty$ tends to 1 as absorption
  vanishes.
* **Eq. 16** behaves as if the layer gave back more light than it received, $m_e(1+m_e)/2
  \approx 4.6\,\%$ more at zero absorption. When absorption is weaker than that, no
  reflectance satisfies the equation (its discriminant is negative). This happens exactly
  where real leaves are brightest, in the near-infrared plateau, where only the baseline and a
  little water absorb.

`liberty` replaces Eq. 16 with the correct sum and changes nothing else (Eqs. 1–9, 17, 19 and
Benford's thickness interpolation). The unit tests check its $R_\infty$ against the Eq. 15
series summed term by term, and check that it conserves energy (R + T ≤ 1) everywhere.

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Reflectance (left) and transmittance (right) of a bright leaf (low baseline absorption) from the corrected `liberty` (green) and the published `liberty_dawson` (gray, dashed), as `xu` (slider) increases. Up to xu = 0.04 both are defined; from 0.06 the published curve breaks wherever its R∞ equation has no solution. The corrected model is defined everywhere and saturates smoothly."
xus = [0.02, 0.03, 0.04, 0.06, 0.08, 0.1, 0.15, 0.2]
fig = make_subplots(rows=1, cols=2, horizontal_spacing=0.09)
start = 2
for k, xu in enumerate(xus):
    th = {**BRIGHT, "xu": xu}
    for model, col, dash, lab in ((fixed, C_FIX, "solid", MODEL_LABEL["liberty"]),
                                  (pub, C_PUB, "dash", MODEL_LABEL["liberty_dawson"])):
        with np.errstate(invalid="ignore"):
            R, T = model.simulate(th)
        for c, y in ((1, R), (2, T)):
            fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=model.wavelength, y=y, mode="lines", line=dict(color=col, width=2, dash=dash),
                                     name=lab, legendgroup=lab, showlegend=(c == 1 and k == start),
                                     visible=(k == start), hovertemplate="%{x} nm: %{y:.3f}<extra>" + lab + "</extra>"),
                          1, c)
n = 4
steps = [dict(method="update", label=f"{xu}", args=[{"visible": [j // n == k for j in range(n * len(xus))]}])
         for k, xu in enumerate(xus)]
fig.update_layout(sliders=[dict(active=start, steps=steps, currentvalue=dict(prefix="xu: "))], height=460,
                  legend=dict(orientation="h", y=1.1))
fig.update_xaxes(title_text="wavelength (nm)")
fig.update_yaxes(title_text="reflectance", range=[0, 0.8], col=1)
fig.update_yaxes(title_text="transmittance", range=[0, 0.8], col=2)
show(fig)
```

## Where each model is defined

At a single wavelength, $R_\infty$ depends only on `xu` and the cell absorption coefficient $k$
at that wavelength. The maps below show that plane at 800 nm for both variants.

* **Published:** the gray region is where the equation has no solution. The prior bound
  `xu ≤ 0.06` (dotted) was needed only to keep fits out of it.
* **Corrected:** there is no gray region. The bound is now 0.2 (dashed), above which NIR
  reflectance changes by less than 2 %.
* **Pilot fits:** the points are the posterior medians of the corrected-model pilot fits
  (their `xu`, and $k$ at each leaf's least-absorbing band).

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "R∞ at 800 nm over (xu, cell absorption coefficient k), contours every 0.1. Left: published LIBERTY (gray: no solution). Right: corrected LIBERTY, with pilot posterior medians coloured by whether the fit passed the convergence screen."
xg = np.linspace(0.005, 0.2, 140)
kg = np.geomspace(1e-3, 3, 160)
X, Kk = np.meshgrid(xg, kg)
fig = make_subplots(rows=1, cols=2, horizontal_spacing=0.08, shared_yaxes=True,
                    subplot_titles=["published (liberty_dawson)", "corrected (liberty)"])
for c, model in ((1, pub), (2, fixed)):
    R = rinf_plane(model, X, Kk)
    if c == 1:
        fig.add_trace(go.Heatmap(x=xg, y=kg, z=np.where(np.isnan(R), 1.0, np.nan), showscale=False,
                                 hoverinfo="skip", colorscale=[[0, "#d9d9d6"], [1, "#d9d9d6"]]), 1, 1)
    fig.add_trace(go.Contour(x=xg, y=kg, z=R, colorscale=[[0, "#e8f1fc"], [1, "#0d366b"]], zmin=0, zmax=1,
                             contours=dict(start=0.1, end=0.9, size=0.1, showlabels=True,
                                           labelfont=dict(size=10, color=SURFACE)),
                             line=dict(width=1, color=SURFACE), showscale=(c == 2),
                             colorbar=dict(title="R∞", len=0.8),
                             hovertemplate="xu %{x:.3f}<br>k %{y:.3g}<br>R∞ %{z:.3f}<extra></extra>"), 1, c)
fig.add_vline(x=0.06, line=dict(color=INK2, width=1.5, dash="dot"), row=1, col=1)
fig.add_vline(x=0.2, line=dict(color=INK2, width=1.5, dash="dash"), row=1, col=2)
if len(fits):
    f = fits.copy()
    C = np.stack([f[a].to_numpy() for a in ABSORBERS], axis=1)
    f["k_min"] = (fixed.fixed["D"] * (f["baseline"].to_numpy()[:, None] + C @ fixed.K.T)).min(axis=1)
    f = f.merge(screen[["observation_id", "run_id", "usable"]], on=["observation_id", "run_id"], how="left") \
        if len(screen) else f.assign(usable=True)
    for ok, col, lab in ((True, "#1baf7a", "pilot fit: usable"), (False, "#eb6834", "pilot fit: excluded")):
        g = f[f["usable"].fillna(False) == ok]
        if len(g):
            fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=g["xu"], y=g["k_min"], mode="markers", name=lab,
                                     marker=dict(size=9, color=col, line=dict(color=SURFACE, width=1.5)),
                                     text=g["observation_id"] + " · " + g["run_id"],
                                     hovertemplate="%{text}<br>xu %{x:.4f}<br>k %{y:.3g}<extra></extra>"), 1, 2)
fig.update_xaxes(title_text="xu")
fig.update_layout(height=520, legend=dict(orientation="h", y=1.15))
log_axis(fig, "y", kg, row=1, col=1, title="cell absorption coefficient k")
log_axis(fig, "y", kg, row=1, col=2)
show(fig)
```

## What the bug did to the fits

The first pilot run fitted the published model, before this bug was found. Bright leaves pulled
their posteriors against the edge of the gray region, and two things went wrong.

* **The sampler hit the wall.** Every Hamiltonian Monte Carlo trajectory that crossed into the
  gray region met an undefined likelihood and counted as a divergent transition. In 64 fits,
  22 had R̂ > 1.05, and up to 98 % of transitions diverged. After all other sampler fixes,
  fits whose posterior touched the wall (smallest discriminant over draws ≤ 0.004) still
  diverged on 27–86 % of transitions. Fits away from the wall had almost none.
* **Fits were pinned at the edge.** Published LIBERTY cannot reach the NIR reflectance of many
  fresh leaves, so it underfitted them, and the other parameters compensated.

Smaller sampler steps did not help: even `target_accept` 0.99 cut divergences on a test leaf
only from 75 % to 68 %. Those fits have been deleted. Every LIBERTY result on this site comes
from the corrected model.

The corrected model is not a drop-in replacement for parameter values. At the same parameters
it transmits about 15–30 % less than the published model and reflects slightly less, so values
calibrated with Eq. 16, including Dawson et al.'s Table 1, do not carry over.

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Observed vs fitted reflectance averaged over 800–900 nm (posterior median fit of the corrected LIBERTY), for pilot leaves. Points below the 1:1 line would be leaves the model cannot make bright enough."
if len(fits) and "nir_obs" in fits:
    f = fits.merge(screen[["observation_id", "run_id", "usable"]], on=["observation_id", "run_id"], how="left") \
        if len(screen) else fits.assign(usable=True)
    fig = go.Figure()
    one_to_one(fig, 0, 0.8)
    for ok, col, lab in ((True, "#1baf7a", "usable"), (False, "#eb6834", "excluded")):
        g = f[f["usable"].fillna(False) == ok]
        if len(g):
            fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=g["nir_obs"], y=g["nir_fit"], mode="markers", name=lab,
                                     marker=dict(size=9, color=col, line=dict(color=SURFACE, width=1.5)),
                                     text=g["observation_id"] + " · " + g["run_id"],
                                     hovertemplate="%{text}<br>observed %{x:.3f}<br>fitted %{y:.3f}<extra></extra>"))
    fig.update_layout(xaxis_title="observed reflectance, 800–900 nm", yaxis_title="LIBERTY fit, 800–900 nm",
                      height=460, legend=dict(orientation="h", y=1.1))
    show(fig)
else:
    no_data("No LIBERTY fits in this fit set yet.")
```

## A second correction: the internal reflectance $m_i$

LIBERTY needs two reflectances of the cell surface: $m_e$, for light arriving from outside the
cell (Eq. 1), and $m_i$, for light inside the cell (Eq. 2). $m_i$ averages the Fresnel
reflectance of light inside the cell over internal angles up to the critical angle. Beyond the
critical angle, all light is totally internally reflected.

`rrtm` had two errors in $m_i$:

* It evaluated the reflectance of light arriving from *outside* at those angles, pairing each
  angle with its refraction into the cell instead of out of it.
* It summed whole degrees only, so it missed the rise to total internal reflection just below
  the critical angle.

Both variants here use the closed forms $m_e = 1 - t_{av}(90°, n)$ and
$m_i = 1 - t_{av}(90°, n)/n^2$, with Stern's (1964) diffuse transmissivity $t_{av}$. These
equal Eqs. 1–2 exactly, which the tests check by numerical quadrature. At 800 nm, $m_i$
changes from 0.541 to 0.564. Unlike Eq. 16, this was an implementation error in `rrtm`, not
in the paper, so `liberty_dawson` includes this correction too.
